Court officials and craftspeople serving early Egyptian kings may have been sacrificed when their ruler died, according to research that found fractures in several ancient skulls.

The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa’ab near Abydos features the tombs and enclosures of the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt, and dates as far back as 3,000BC.

rfi.title: US top diplomat Rubio says West must choose ‘national power’ or decline
rfi.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a combative defence of Washington’s right to wield its “national power” in Athens on Wednesday, while urging Europe to “awaken from its long slumber”.

rfi.title: ‘I became their slave’: Israeli hostage recounts 500 days in Hamas captivity
rfi.description: Omer Shem Tov was abducted by Hamas at the Nova music festival in Israel on 7 October, 2023 and held hostage by the armed Islamist group for 505 days. The 24-year-old has published a book about his time in captivity, entitled Meeting Myself in Hell. RFI spoke to him at his parents' home near Tel Aviv.

rfi.title: Three years on from the 7 October attacks, war has redrawn the map of Palestine
rfi.description: More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in the war launched by Israel following the 7 October, 2023 Hamas attacks. Palestinian territory has also become increasingly fragmented – in Gaza, the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem.

rfi.title: Franco-Japanese duo Kagan and Soai win 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry
rfi.description: The Nobel Prize in chemistry was awarded on Wednesday to French scientist Henri B. Kagan and Japan’s Kenso Soai for unravelling the mystery of why only one of two forms of certain molecules occurs in nature.

rfi.title: France's Prime Minister Lecornu to address the nation over student protests
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will address the nation on Wednesday evening as part of his government's drive to end the wave of student blockades, which have closed high schools throughout the country.

rfi.title: African Union to launch continent's first credit rating agency in Mauritius
rfi.description: The African Union is launching the continent’s first credit rating agency on Wednesday, aiming to provide an alternative to the global “big three” by drawing on African expertise and perspectives.

rfi.title: Malian army retakes strategic city of Kidal after Tuareg separatists withdraw
rfi.description: The Malian army and its Russian allies entered the strategic northern city of Kidal on Tuesday without resistance after Tuareg separatists announced a tactical withdrawal, five months after government forces were driven out.

rfi.title: France earmarks a further €7m to help fight DRC's worst-ever Ebola crisis
rfi.description: France has decided to allocate an additional €7 million this year to combat the Ebola epidemic currently ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This comes as Kenya announced its first-ever death from the disease.

rfi.title: EU suspends beef exports from Namibia due to foot and mouth disease
rfi.description: The largest market for Namibian beef, the European Union, announced it has suspended imports after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, which wreaked havoc in Europe 25 years ago.

rfi.title: French MEP Hassan under investigation over flag incident at 7 October commemoration
rfi.description: Hard-left French EU lawmaker Rima Hassan is facing an investigation after the Israeli and European Union flags were allegedly thrown to the floor at a commemoration for the 2023 Hamas attacks that set off the Gaza war. Hassan said the action was to denounce the "ongoing genocide by the Israeli government".

rfi.title: Quebec separatist party wins provincial election in test of Canada's unity
rfi.description: Separatists won provincial elections in Quebec on Monday, with a promise to hold a vote on leaving Canada after US President Donald Trump leaves office, testing Prime Minister Mark Carney's message of national unity.

rfi.title: Argentina boss Scaloni salutes 'inimitable' Messi after maestro's final game
rfi.description: Argentina’s head coach Lionel Scaloni hailed the enduring genius of the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain striker Lionel Messi on Wednesday moments after the 39-year-old played his last game for the national team.

rfi.title: French PM slams violence at student protests and promises 'timeout' for democracy
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said there can be "no room for tolerance of violence", as tens of thousands of students took to the streets nationwide on Tuesday to protest over the state of schools. He told parliament that high schools would clear their schedules for the rest of the week to create space for democratic debate and air grievances.

rfi.title: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests
rfi.description: Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected on the streets of Paris on Tuesday as France's powerful trade unions join high school students rallying for better conditions in a wave of protests marked by clashes with police.

rfi.title: Olise strikes twice in France's romp past Belgium in Nations League
rfi.description: Désiré Doué, Ryan Cherki and two goals from Michael Olise launched the late pyrotechnics on Monday night at the Stade de France as France scored four times in 13 minutes to whoosh past Belgium 4-1 and maintain the lead of their Nations League pool.

rfi.title: Lebanon joined by UK and France for three weeks of joint military drills
rfi.description: Lebanon's army will hold three weeks of exercises with the British military from Tuesday, both sides said on Monday, with the drills to involve personnel and representatives from countries including France, Italy and the United States.

rfi.title: Climate change driving child marriages and teen pregnancies, study finds
rfi.description: The charity Plan International said on Monday that global warming has increased the risk of child marriages, teenage pregnancies and violence against girls. Its report coincides with talks in the South Pacific nations of Fiji and Tuvalu, where climate change is affecting all aspects of daily life.

rfi.title: Study shows extreme poverty and homelessness on the rise in France
rfi.description: An international study published on Monday by France’s largest food aid charity, Restos du Cœur, shows the number of people living in extreme poverty in France and other wealthy countries increased by 37 percent between 2018 and 2025.

euronews.title: Russian man who swam from Kaliningrad to Lithuania in asylum attempt sentenced to six years hard labour
euronews.description: A 68-year-old Russian man who swam across the Nemunas River from Russia's Kaliningrad exclave into neighbouring Lithuania in an attempt to seek asylum has been sentenced to six years in a strict-regime penal colony in Russia for "publicly justifying terrorism."

euronews.description: In a televised address from his official residence the French prime minister acknowledges young people anger 'doesn't come from nowhere' and promises a plan to respond to the crisis

euronews.description: Haruka Kaju extended her unbeaten World Judo Tour run to 40 contests, defending her -63kg world title against Kerem Primo. At -81kg, Tato Grigalashvili defeated home favourite Zelim Tckaev to claim his fourth world title and return to the top of the podium.

euronews.title: Southern right whales return to South Africa, drawing crowds to the coast
euronews.description: Southern right whales return to Hermanus, South Africa, drawing crowds to the cliffs and whale festival as mothers nurse newborn calves in Walker Bay.

euronews.title: Maricarmen, symbol of Spain's housing protests, dies
euronews.description: The 87-year-old woman had withstood four eviction attempts in the past decade. In a final message from her hospital bed, she urged protesters: "Fight!"

euronews.description: The US president says the Mexican leader rang him to urge him not to rename the Gulf of Mexico. Trump justified the change with coastal data that available figures do not support.

euronews.title: Rubio in Athens urges Europe to shoulder more of its defence burden
euronews.description: The US secretary of state held talks on energy, military cooperation and regional security, pointing to Greece as an example of higher defence spending. The agenda also included LNG, F-35s, the Eastern Mediterranean and the Strait of Hormuz.

euronews.title: Knife attack at Polish school: in Ostroleka a student injures seven, two are in critical condition
euronews.description: On Wednesday morning at a vocational school in Ostrołęka in Northern Poland, a 19-year-old pupil attacked classmates and teachers with a sharp tool, injuring seven people, two of whom are in a serious condition, police said.

euronews.title: Fantasy worlds come to life on nails at London nail art competition
euronews.description: Nailympia London showcased fantasy nail art inspired by folklore, forests and steampunk, as global artists raced to create miniature worlds on nails.

euronews.description: Hailed as the most technologically advanced and powerful Jaguar in the company’s history, it premiered in New York today, targeting a younger, wealthier and mostly American customer base.

euronews.description: Brocade carries centuries of Chinese history, woven with patterns that have long held meanings beyond decoration. Now, the traditional craft is finding a new expression on the Milan catwalk, as designers reinterpret the fabric for a contemporary audience.

euronews.title: Russia dismisses transparency calls amid reports of second Siberia plague case
euronews.description: Rospotrebnadzor said nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous pathogens and saw "no epidemic risk," while the Kremlin called most media reporting "false" and said it had no knowledge of a US demarche formally requesting additional information.

euronews.title: Deadly drone attacks raise questions over Europe’s Black Sea defences
euronews.description: The European Union has a plan to safeguard the Black Sea. But days after drones wreaked havoc along Romania and Bulgaria’s coast, sinking commercial vessels and killing two people, questions loom over how Brussels can protect the sea.

euronews.title: ‘We will certainly look at it’: Trump says he will consider permanent US military base in Lithuania
euronews.description: US President Donald Trump said he would consider Lithuania’s proposal to permanently host US troops after the Baltic country said it was ready to accommodate a permanent American military presence.

euronews.title: Residents search belongings after Jerusalem building demolished
euronews.description: A five-storey building in Jerusalem’s al-Tur was demolished by Israeli authorities over alleged lack of permits, displacing dozens of Palestinian residents.

lemonde.title: Face au mouvement lycéen, le gouvernement se donne du temps, au risque de l’enlisement
lemonde.description: A l’approche des vacances scolaires, qui débutent le 17 octobre, le premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, a annoncé que « les premières décisions du gouvernement seront présentées à la fin du mois ».

lemonde.title: Carburants : Sébastien Lecornu annonce que 10 millions de barils de gazole seront mis à la disposition des distributeurs et espère une baisse des prix comprise « entre 12 à 18 centimes » le litre à la pompe
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre a annoncé qu’il réunirait à Matignon les distributeurs « pour y travailler dans les tout prochains jours ».

lemonde.title: Comment le Kremlin orchestre la reprise des actifs russes de Leroy-Merlin, d’Auchan, de Nestlé et de FM Logistic
lemonde.description: Vladimir Poutine a déclaré que ces magasins pourraient revenir à leurs propriétaires occidentaux. Dans les faits, par le biais d’une société-écran, Moscou en organise la confiscation. Après la mise « sous administration temporaire » devrait venir la répartition de ces actifs entre sociétés amies.

lemonde.title: A Elne, dans les Pyrénées-Orientales, le maire d’extrême droite débaptise le cinéma René-Vautier, nom jugé trop « politique »
lemonde.description: Le retrait du nom du militant anticolonialiste n’est pas un cas isolé. Il fait écho à la reprise en main de la salle de Bruay-la-Buissière, dans le Pas-de-Calais, par le maire RN Ludovic Pajot.

lemonde.title: « On est encore au Moyen Age » : dans l’e-sport, les femmes en première ligne des violences sexistes et sexuelles
lemonde.description: Un streameur et commentateur réputé de « League of Legends » a été mis en examen en juillet pour viol, selon les informations du « Monde ». Un cas révélateur des violences sexuelles qui n’épargnent pas l’e-sport, un secteur très masculin au sein duquel la parole des femmes peine à être écoutée.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, le réveil d’une gauche socialiste et démocrate, portée par une nouvelle génération d’élus et de militants
lemonde.description: Galvanisée par des figures comme Bernie Sanders et Zohran Mamdani, une « nouvelle gauche » est en essor aux Etats-Unis et attire de nombreux jeunes. Les candidats de cette mouvance, trentenaires ou quadragénaires, espèrent remporter des victoires décisives aux midterms du 3 novembre.

lemonde.title: Un traitement optogénétique redonne une vision partielle à six patients aveugles
lemonde.description: Un essai clinique, mené chez dix personnes non voyantes en France, aux Etats-Unis et au Royaume-Uni, suggère l’intérêt, pour restaurer une forme de vision, d’un traitement qui consiste à injecter dans l’œil un vecteur viral porteur d’une construction génétique.

lemonde.title: En Israël, trois ans après le 7-Octobre, les traumatismes et les aveuglements d’un pays
lemonde.description: En pleine campagne électorale, l’Etat hébreu entamait la commémoration, mardi, des victimes de l’attaque terroriste du Hamas. Depuis le drame, le pays poursuit une guerre sans fin motivée par un désir de vengeance, sans s’interroger sur les failles qui ont conduit au désastre.

lemonde.title: Christa Pike, qui a survécu à son exécution aux Etats-Unis, a repris connaissance et se dit « en colère et désorientée »
lemonde.description: Seule condamnée à avoir survécu à une injection létale aux Etats-Unis, la quinquagénaire reste menottée à son lit d’hôpital, selon ses avocats.

lemonde.title: Crise du logement en Espagne : l’octogénaire expulsée à l’origine du mouvement de protestation est morte
lemonde.description: Maricarmen Abascal, 87 ans, avait été hospitalisée dans un état d’épuisement après son expulsion, bien qu’un accord ait été obtenu avec la société propriétaire pour qu’elle puisse réintégrer son appartement.

lemonde.title: Apologie du terrorisme : trois mineurs en garde à vue à Orléans après une vidéo dans un lycée, mentionnant les attaques de Mohammed Merah et Salah Abdeslam
lemonde.description: Sur les images, les lycées sont vus en train de reprendre un morceau de rap faisant référence aux attaques terroristes. Par ailleurs, une enquête a été ouverte en Vendée en raison d’une vidéo dans laquelle des adolescents diffusent ce même morceau, dans une église.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : le RN veut supprimer les intercommunalités
lemonde.description: Le Rassemblement national a présenté un contre-budget pour 2027 et une trajectoire financière pour le prochain quinquennat. Marine Le Pen, en cas de victoire à la présidentielle, attend un effort de 8,2 milliards d’euros des collectivités locales dès l’an prochain.

lemonde.title: Fabien Roussel accuse le gouvernement israélien de « terrorisme d’Etat »
lemonde.description: Le candidat communiste à la présidentielle a également condamné, sur LCI, les attaques du Hamas du 7 octobre 2023. Il renvoie dos à dos le gouvernement de Benyamin Nétanyahou et le mouvement islamiste palestinien en dénonçant « des forces extrémistes qui s’affrontent et qui sèment la haine ».

lemonde.title: Donald Trump veut faire d’un de ses complexes de golf une résidence présidentielle officielle
lemonde.description: La Maison Blanche étudie la possibilité de transformer une des luxueuses propriétés que Donald Trump possède en Floride en retraite sécurisée à l’usage des futurs présidents américains. Brouillant encore la frontière entre le mandat du chef de l’Etat et ses intérêts privés.

lemonde.title: L’Arabie saoudite déplore trois morts dans des attaques houthistes contre des aéroports
lemonde.description: Les combattants houthistes, opposés au gouvernement yéménite soutenu par l’Arabie saoudite, ont revendiqué, mercredi, des tirs de missiles et de drones visant l’aéroport international de Riyad et celui d’Abha. Des ressortissants égyptien, algérien et soudanais ont péri et 36 autres personnes ont été blessées.

lemonde.title: L’ouverture d’une base chinoise au Laos, après l’installation d’une autre au Cambodge, inquiète les pays de la région
lemonde.description: Avec la création d’un centre de formation de pilotes sur la base rénovée de Ban Keun, le Laos devient le second pays d’Asie du Sud-Est, après le Cambodge, à accueillir une infrastructure d’entraînement militaire conjointe avec la Chine.

france24fr.title: La mort de Mariecarmen à Madrid, un "meurtre dû à la spéculation immobilière"
france24fr.description: Mariecarmen, dont l'expulsion a entraîné un mouvement citoyen contre la crise du logement en Espagne, est décédée à l'hôpital mercredi, rapporte la correspondante de France 24 à Madrid, Maude Petit-Jové. Les manifestants, rassemblés sur la Puerta del Sol pour dénoncer la spéculation immobilière, l'ont appris en pleine AG. Après une minute de silence, ils ont dénoncé des "meurtres". Le mouvement se poursuit : la grève générale est prévue le 11 novembre.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : les démocrates poursuivent Trump pour des publicités payées par les contribuables
france24fr.description: Le Comité national du Parti démocrate (DNC) a déposé une plainte, mercredi, contre le président américain Donald Trump. Il l'accuse de "violation flagrante" de l'interdiction de s'approprier des fonds publics pour des publicités à sa gloire, et notamment en période électorale.

france24fr.title: "Plus jamais Bolsonaro" : des milliers de manifestants mobilisés avant le second tour au Brésil
france24fr.description: Portant des autocollants proclamant par exemple "Non au père, non au fils", des milliers de Brésiliens ont participé mercredi à la manifestation convoquée à Rio de Janeiro par des organisations étudiantes. Ils appellent à faire barrage au sénateur conservateur Flavio Bolsonaro, arrivé en tête au premier tour face au président sortant Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

france24fr.title: Gaza : plus de 8 bâtiments sur 10 endommagés ou détruits
france24fr.description: Après l’attaque menée par le Hamas le 7 octobre 2023, Israël a lancé une offensive avec plusieurs objectifs affichés : ramener les otages, démanteler les capacités militaires du Hamas et faire en sorte que Gaza ne puisse plus constituer une menace pour Israël. Trois ans après, le moins que l'on puisse dire c'est que l'enclave palestinienne n'a plus du tout le même visage.

france24fr.title: Nostalgie, résilience et tensions politiques : Israël rend hommage aux victimes du 7-Octobre
france24fr.description: Israël a commémoré mercredi les attaques du Hamas survenues sur son territoire le 7 octobre 2023, dont le souvenir pèse sur la campagne des élections législatives. Civils et proches des victimes se sont recueillis sur le site du festival de musique électronique Nova, où 348 jeunes gens avaient été exécutés par les activistes du Hamas, mais aussi à Tel-Aviv.

france24fr.title: Russie : les soupçons de peste contaminent les réseaux sociaux
france24fr.description: La Russie est appelée, de la part de l'OMS, de l'Union européenne et des Etats-Unis, à plus de transparence après la mort d'une technicienne de laboratoire en Sibérie. Daria Shipilova, qui travaillait à l'institut de lutte contre la peste d'Irkutsk, est décédée d'une pneumonie dont l'origine est indéterminée. Entre les versions de certains médias et le démenti des autorités, le flou persiste et entretient rumeurs et désinformation.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie: des troupes érythréennes se déploient dans le nord du Tigré
france24fr.description: Des troupes érythréennes se déploient ces derniers jours autour d'Adigrat, dans le nord de l'État régional éthiopien du Tigré, frontalier de l'Érythrée, vers laquelle des forces éthiopiennes semblent se diriger, ont indiqué mercredi des sources concordantes, sur fond de tensions exacerbées entre Éthiopie et Érythrée.

france24fr.title: Espagne : Maricarmen, la retraitée devenue symbole de la crise du logement, est morte
france24fr.description: Maricarmen, une femme de 87 ans, avait été expulsée de son appartement à Madrid le 23 septembre. Dans la foulée, des milliers de personnes étaient descendues dans la rue pour manifester contre la crise du logement en Espagne. La retraitée est morte mercredi, a annoncé un syndicat de locataires.

france24fr.title: Mali : après Kidal, quelles perspectives pour l'armée dans le nord ?
france24fr.description: 🇲🇱 La reprise de Kidal marque un tournant pour l’armée malienne, après sept mois de revers. Les FAMA ont repris cette ville stratégique sans combat, à la suite du repli des Touaregs du FLA. Reste désormais à consolider ce succès dans le Nord.

france24fr.title: 7-Octobre : quel avenir pour Israël ?
france24fr.description: Trois ans après l’attaque du 7 octobre 2023 en Israël, la plus meurtrière jamais perpétrée dans le pays par le Hamas, des commémorations se sont tenues tout au long de la journée. Cette attaque avait déclenché une vaste offensive israélienne dans la bande de Gaza. Cet anniversaire intervient cette année dans un contexte politique particulièrement tendu, à l’approche des élections législatives.

france24fr.title: Lecornu joue l'apaisement avec les lycéens et annonce des mesures sur le prix de l'essence
france24fr.description: Sébastien Lecornu a tenté d'apporter des réponses à plusieurs crises mercredi lors d'une allocution, assurant que les forces de l'ordre "n'ont pas pour instruction d'affronter les lycéens", affirmant ne "pas être indifférent à leurs angoisses" et annonçant par ailleurs une mesure permettant une baisse de 12 à 18 centimes du prix du litre à la pompe.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : "Les forces de l'ordre n'ont pas pour instruction d'affronter les lycéens", dit Sébastien Lecornu
Mouvement lycéen : la France dénonce une campagne de "désinformation" iranienne
france24fr.description: Le ministère français des Affaires étrangères a convoqué mercredi l'ambassadeur iranien à Paris pour dénoncer la "campagne de désinformation" que la France accuse l'Iran de mener au sujet du mouvement lycéen. Paris qualifie aussi d'"infondée" la convocation la veille par Téhéran de l'ambassadeur de France en Iran.

france24fr.title: L'Australie, future présidente de la COP, pourtant toujours très dépendante du charbon
france24fr.description: L'Australie s'apprête à diriger les négociations de la COP31 Climat. Mais le pays est rattrapé par l'actualité: sa Haute Cour de Justice vient de s'opposer à l'extension d'une mine de charbon, trop dangereuse pour le climat. Une décision qui met en lumière la très grande dépendance du pays au charbon. Il représente 9% du PIB australien. Une production massivement exportée, ce qui permet à l'Australie de présenter un bilan d'émissions en baisse tout en augmentant sa production de charbon

france24fr.title: Aux Comores, une nouvelle loi inquiète la communauté malgache
france24fr.description: Aux Comores, une nouvelle loi, votée mais pas encore appliquée, réserve certaines activités de petit commerce aux seuls Comoriens de naissance. Une mesure qui inquiète vivement la communauté malgache installée dans l'archipel. Récit de Maya-Anaïs Yataghène.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : la France offre des drones à l'armée malgache
france24fr.description: Catherine Vautrin, ministre française des Armées, était ce mardi à Madagascar pour une visite de quelques heures. Elle y a annoncé un don de drones à l'armée malgache, alors que la Grande Île s'est rapprochée de Moscou depuis l'arrivée des militaires au pouvoir il y a un an. Correspondance d'Aurélie Kouman.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : le redécoupage électoral peut-il faire basculer le Congrès ?
france24fr.description: À l’approche des élections de mi-mandat, les redécoupages électoraux sont au cœur de la bataille entre républicains et démocrates. Quel impact le "gerrymandering "peut-il avoir sur les résultats et le contrôle de la Chambre des représentants ? Décryptage avec Jérôme Viala-Godefroy, chargé de cours à Sciences Po, et Matthieu Mabin, correspondant de France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : une frappe russe sur un immeuble fait 18 morts à Prylouky
france24fr.description: De nouvelles frappes de missiles russes touchent l’Ukraine : à Prylouky, un immeuble a été frappé, faisant 18 morts. Une nouvelle attaque meurtrière contre une zone résidentielle, racontée par Ludovic de Foucaud.

nzz.title: Die 87-jährige Spanierin Maricarmen Abascal stirbt zwei Wochen nach Zwangsräumung
nzz.description: Das Schicksal der Spanierin Maricarmen Abascal, die nach siebzig Jahren von der Polizei aus ihrer Wohnung geholt wurde, hat Massenproteste ausgelöst. Was viele befürchtet hatten, ist eingetreten.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Christa Pike überlebte zwei Todesspritzen. Nun ist sie wieder bei Bewusstsein – Das Wichtigste zum misslungenen Hinrichtungsversuch in den USA
nzz.description: Die zum Tode verurteilte Mörderin hätte schmerzfrei sterben sollen – stattdessen wird sie nun im Spital behandelt. Wie Fachleute sich die gescheiterte Exekution erklären.

nzz.title: «Wo bin ich, und wer seid ihr?» – Christa Pike spricht erstmals nach gescheitertem Hinrichtungsversuch
nzz.description: Die Mörderin Christa Pike überlebte bei ihrem Hinrichtungsversuch zwei Dosen Pentobarbital. Nun ist sie wieder bei Bewusstsein, doch ihr Gesundheitszustand bleibt kritisch.

nzz.title: Die Ski-WM 2027 in Crans-Montana kommen nicht zur Ruhe – nun tritt der OK-Präsident zurück
nzz.description: Die Staatsanwaltschaft hat gegen Claude-Alain Schmidhalter eine Anklage erhoben. Mit den Heim-WM 2027 hat das zwar wenig zu tun, doch es passt ins Bild: Seit Beginn wird die Organisation von allerlei Wirren begleitet.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Zwei Verletzte nach Explosion in Olten
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Lehre vom Müllcontainer auf dem Nova-Festivalgelände: Wer Israel helfen will, muss seine Sicherheitsinteressen wahren
nzz.description: Der Terrorangriff vom 7. Oktober hat die israelische Gesellschaft fundamental verändert. Die Erfahrung der Ohnmacht hat die Bereitschaft, Sicherheitsrisiken einzugehen, radikal reduziert. Israels Partner müssen ihre Politik an diese neue Realität anpassen.

nzz.title: Ein Triumph für die Tessiner SVP: Piero Marchesi als Nachfolger von Claudio Zali vereidigt
nzz.description: Im Kanton Tessin zieht erstmals ein SVP-Politiker in den Staatsrat ein. Die Partei wird in der Südschweiz immer stärker.

nzz.title: Mehr streiten, günstiger bauen: Zürichs neuer Hochbauvorsteher Tobias Langenegger setzt einen unerwarteten Schwerpunkt
nzz.description: Für den SP-Stadtrat ist die grösste Erkenntnis nach den ersten Monaten, wie schnell er in diesem Amt etwas verändern kann. Er weiss auch, wozu er diese Macht nutzen will.

nzz.title: «Putsch gegen die direkte Demokratie»: Das Parlament will kantonale Mindestlöhne übersteuern, nun lancieren die Gewerkschaften den Abstimmungskampf
nzz.description: Der Mindestlohn ist ein politischer Dauerbrenner in der Schweiz. Die Befürworter wollen damit die Kaufkraft stärken. Die Gegner sehen darin eine Schwächung der erfolgreichen Sozialpartnerschaft.

nzz.title: Nun protestiert die Jugend auch in Belgien – der Verteidigungsminister will sie mit der Wehrpflicht disziplinieren
nzz.description: Die französischen Schülerproteste sind auf Belgien übergeschwappt. Die Polizei hat sogar 13-Jährige festgenommen. Die Regierung verteidigt derweil ihren Sparkurs im Bildungsbereich.

nzz.title: Schülerproteste in Frankreich: Die Gewalt setzt Präsident Macron unter Druck
nzz.description: Nach schweren Verletzungen von Jugendlichen schränkt die französische Regierung den Einsatz von Polizeigranaten ein. Zugleich sollen Gespräche an den Schulen die Proteste beruhigen. Doch die Jugendlichen wollen weitermachen.

nzz.title: Auch Moleküle können links oder rechts sein, mit teilweise gefährlichen Konsequenzen: Der Chemienobelpreis geht an zwei Forscher aus Frankreich und Japan
nzz.description: Henri Kagan und Kenso Soai haben Reaktionen entdeckt, mit denen man selektiv nur eine dieser spiegelbildlichen Varianten herstellen kann. Das ist wichtig für die Entwicklung von Medikamenten.

nzz.title: Er ist bodenständig und macht die Drecksarbeit: Harry Kane steigt in neue Sphären auf
nzz.description: Harry Kane ist neu Rekordspieler der englischen Nationalmannschaft, er zieht mit der Goalie-Legende Peter Shilton gleich und wird mit Standing Ovations geehrt. Die nächste Krönung könnte Ende Oktober bei der Verleihung des Ballon d’Or folgen.

nzz.title: Die SVP Schwyz nominiert den etwas ratlosen Herrn Rüegsegger für die Nachfolge von Guy Parmelin
nzz.description: Regierungsrat André Rüegsegger hat sich noch gar nicht für eine Kandidatur entschieden. Der Testballon soll das Karussell in Bewegung bringen.

nzz.title: Ein Ex-Polizist wartet in einer Januarnacht bewaffnet in einem Zürcher Wohnquartier. Als eine Streife ihn kontrollieren will, drückt er ab
nzz.description: Auf wen hatte der Mazedonier mit geladener Pistole gewartet? Der Prozess am Bezirksgericht Dielsdorf führt zu einer Spionageaffäre auf dem Balkan.

zeit.title: Nach der Wahl in Berlin: Regierungsbildung in Berlin – wie geht es weiter?
Gemütlichkeit und Wärme: Brennholz in Hessen: Was Kaminofenbesitzer wissen sollten
Neue Show in Stuttgart: Julia lässt Romeo hinter sich – Musical startet in Stuttgart
Sachsen-Anhalt: Stimmen für AfD? Radtke fordert Parteiausschlussverfahren
Friedliche Revolution: Einheitsdenkmal: Skulpturen sollen vier Meter groß werden
Viren: Grippezeit beginnt: So ist die Lage in Hessen
Zeitmessung: Der Schaltsekunde steht das Aus bevor
Friedensbewegung: 40 Jahre nach Rekordkundgebung: «Bedrohung hat zugenommen»
Europäischer Rechnungshof: Rechnungshof sieht weiter hohe Fehlerquote bei Ausgabe von EU-Geldern
zeit.description: Erneut sind EU-Gelder laut Europäischem Rechnungshof in erheblichem Umfang fehlerhaft verwendet worden. Betroffen waren 2025 nach Schätzungen rund 6,7 Milliarden Euro.

zeit.title: European Product Act: Verbände fordern strengere EU-Regeln für Produkte aus Drittstaaten
zeit.description: Viele Produkte, die über Onlineplattformen aus Drittstaaten importiert werden, verstoßen gegen EU-Regeln. Mehrere Verbände fordern neue Haftungsregeln.

zeit.title: Donald Trump: Demokraten verklagen Trump-Regierung wegen Werbespots
zeit.description: Die US-Demokraten werfen Trump vor, Steuergelder in Millionenhöhe für TV-Spots der Regierung eingesetzt zu haben. Das DNC will die Werbung für unzulässig erklären lassen.

zeit.title: Niedrigwasser: Experten rechnen nicht mit baldiger Erholung des Bodensee-Pegelstandes
zeit.description: Der Bodensee hat in diesem Jahr außergewöhnlich wenig Wasser bekommen. Für eine Erholung bräuchte es überdurchschnittliche Niederschläge im Herbst und Winter.

zeit.title: Hinrichtungsversuch in Tennessee: US-Amerikanerin kann nach überlebter Hinrichtung wieder sprechen
zeit.description: Laut ihren Anwälten ist Christa Pike bei Bewusstsein, »wütend und verwirrt«. Sie fordern, dass nicht noch einmal versucht wird, sie hinzurichten.

zeit.title: Spanien: 87-jährige Spanierin stirbt nach Zwangsräumung in Madrid
zeit.description: María del Carmen Abascal wurde nach ihrer Zwangsräumung zum Symbol der Wohnungskrise in Spanien. Sie hätte in ihre Wohnung zurückkehren dürfen, ist aber gestorben.

zeit.title: Schulproteste in Belgien: Bahnhof in Belgien wegen Schulprotesten zwischenzeitlich geschlossen
zeit.description: Ausschreitungen rund um Schulproteste in Lüttich haben die Polizei dazu veranlasst, einen Bahnhof zu schließen. Die Beamten sprachen von »bedeutenden Unruhen«.

observador.title: As notícias das 2h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 1h. Protestos e vigilias em Espanha após morte de Maricarmen
observador.description: Em frente ao parlamento espanhol, manifestantes gritaram que Maricarmen não morreu, foi assassinada. Ainda nesta edição, Villas Boas pede o bicampeonato e deixa rasgados elogios a Francesco Farioli.

observador.title: Advogados dizem que Christa Pike está "zangada e confusa"
observador.description: Os advogados da reclusa descrevem "confusão cognitiva" e danos físicos graves. Tribunal ordenou a preservação de todas as provas da execução falhada.

observador.title: Caldeira Cabral coordena Livro Branco do Alojamento Local
observador.description: Contributos podem ser enviados até ao final de 2026. Economista defende que "a crise da habitação não pode ser explicada com a criação do Alojamento Local".

observador.title: Viva o povo brasileiro?
observador.description: O que se passa com o povo brasileiro? Deixou-se manipular pela desinformação, pelo populismo, pela demagogia, pelo extremismo, ou foi mesmo interferência externa?

observador.title: Deus nos acuda
observador.description: O Cristianismo, que moldou o Ocidente, pode voltar a ser o seu ai-Jesus?

observador.title: Seguro, o Presidente do futuro
observador.description: O futuro de que o Presidente da República não se cansa de falar é muito semelhante ao futuro publicitário dos slogans e dos cartazes eleitorais, um futuro sem substância.

observador.title: WWF elogia avanços em Portugal mas deixa alertas
observador.description: Lince-ibérico, atum-rabilho e sardinha são casos positivos. Mas transportes, pobreza energética e sistema alimentar travam a recuperação da natureza em Portugal.

observador.title: Norte cria 37 mil empregos e reduz desemprego
observador.description: Construção liderou crescimento do emprego (+11,9%), salário médio subiu para 1.289€ e exportações cresceram 3,9%. Mas agricultura perdeu 9,5 mil postos de trabalho.

observador.title: Um surto de realidade em Nova Iorque
observador.description: O que ocorre, neste momento, em Nova Iorque e na Pensilvânia, não é apenas um surto de sarampo; é uma epidemia de realidade.

observador.title: Menos carros, mais ideologia?
observador.description: A esquerda conseguiu que os seus pressupostos fossem entendidos como neutros e triviais; questioná-los ou contrariá-los passou a ser apontado como excentricidade ideológica.

observador.title: WWF: declínio de 73% das espécies, mas conservação dá frutos
observador.description: Relatório Planeta Vivo 2026 da WWF mantém valor alarmante, mas aponta pela 1ª vez casos concretos de recuperação. Tigre passou de 3.200 para 5.700 exemplares desde 2010.

observador.title: De 248 mil para 101 mil: Manica reduz insegurança alimentar
observador.description: A produção agrícola da campanha 2025-2026 e medidas de irrigação reduziram em 147 mil o número de pessoas em risco — mas a nível nacional o cenário agrava-se.

observador.title: 00h. Trump pondera ataques ao Irão antes das intercalares
observador.description: Fontes da Casa Branca dizem que os ataques podem demonstrar ao eleitorado que Trump quer reduzir os preços dos combustíveis e que estão a ser feitos progressos no conflito antes das eleições.

observador.title: A alienação, segundo Marx
observador.description: O povo estava desorientado no meio do deserto traiçoeiro do capitalismo. Mas veio o profeta e o povo perdido foi conduzido à terra prometida do comunismo, «onde correm o leite e o mel». Que maravilha!

observador.title: É um país de pequenas vaidades e de muitos medos
observador.description: Por razões que desconheço foi permitido a um jogador o título de dono da seleção. Não sei quem tem o direito de atribuir essa propriedade que pertence a todos nós.

observador.title: Heterossexual, branco, católico e talvez fascista!
observador.description: Quando chamar fascista a quem discorda se torna reflexo automático, o efeito não é isolar extremistas: é ensinar milhões de pessoas comuns a calarem-se.

observador.title: O paradoxo da sociedade sem Polícia
observador.description: É mais fácil denunciar os defeitos de uma instituição do que demonstrar que as funções que desempenha podem ser dispensadas sem custos para a sociedade.

spiegel.title: Ukraine meldet 28 Tote bei russischen Angriffen an Putins Geburtstag
spiegel.description: Der Kremlchef ist 74 Jahre alt geworden. Offenbar nahm die russische Armee dies zum Anlass für eine schwere Angriffswelle in der Ukraine – unter anderem auf ein fünfstöckiges Wohnhaus.

spiegel.title: US-Demokraten verklagen Trump wegen Wahlwerbung aus Steuergeldern
spiegel.description: In hinreichend schrägen Werbespots wirbt Donald Trump derzeit um Stimmen bei den Zwischenwahlen – mit dem Disclaimer: »Finanziert von der US-Regierung«. Deshalb schicken die Demokraten jetzt ihre Anwälte los.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Trump-Golfclub in Florida soll Rückzugsort für US-Präsidenten werden
spiegel.description: Liegt das neue Camp David in Florida? Zumindest gibt es den Plan, einen Trump-Golfclub in West Palm Beach für ehemalige und künftige US-Präsidenten zu öffnen. Im Weißen Haus sorgt das für Entzücken.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg: Vier Mopedfahrer sterben bei Verkehrsunfall
spiegel.description: Bei einem schweren Unfall im Barnim sind vier Menschen ums Leben gekommen. Ein Autofahrer erfasste beim Überholen drei entgegenkommende Mopeds. Drei Fahrer und eine Mitfahrerin starben.

spiegel.title: Westjordanland: Palästinenser während der Olivenernte von israelischen Siedlern getötet
spiegel.description: Im besetzten Westjordanland ist ein 44-jähriger Palästinenser bei einem Angriff israelischer Siedler getötet worden. Siedler-Gewalt erschwert palästinensischen Bauern zunehmend den Zugang zu ihren Olivenhainen.

spiegel.title: John Coale: Dreht Donald Trumps Ex-Anwalt jetzt die US-Strategie für Russland?
spiegel.description: John Coale soll offenbar die festgefahrenen Gespräche mit dem Kreml voranbringen. Einem Medienbericht zufolge mit einem Wirtschaftsdeal nach belarussischem Vorbild. Gegen den Willen der Ukraine.

spiegel.title: Saudi-Arabien: Huthi-Miliz bekennt sich zu Angriffen auf Flughäfen in Riad und Abha
spiegel.description: Bei Raketentreffern sind auf zwei Flughäfen in Saudi-Arabien drei Menschen getötet und Dutzende weitere verletzt worden. Die Huthi-Miliz erklärte, sie habe die Attacken ausgeführt.

spiegel.title: Minnesota: FBI vereitelt mutmaßlichen Terroranschlag auf Einkaufszentrum
spiegel.description: Ein 18-Jähriger soll einen Terroranschlag im US-Bundesstaat Minnesota geplant haben. Das FBI nahm den Mann fest, nachdem er von einem verdeckten Ermittler ein Sturmgewehr gekauft hatte. Er wollte wohl bis zu 60 Menschen töten.

spiegel.title: Christa Pike: Anwälte schildern Gesundheitszustand nach gescheiterter Hinrichtung
spiegel.description: Christa Pike leidet nach der missglückten Hinrichtung an einer Lungenentzündung und kann weder essen noch ihre Arme bewegen, so ihr Anwalt. Dieser fordert Zugang zu den Beweismitteln.

spiegel.title: Maricarmen: Spanierin, deren Wohnung zwangsgeräumt wurde, ist tot
spiegel.description: María del Carmen Abascal, die ihre Wohnung zwangsweise verlassen musste, ist im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben. Ihr Fall hatte in Spanien Proteste gegen die Wohnungskrise ausgelöst.

spiegel.title: Salt and Silver: Warum sich die Gründer Riffelmacher und Kosikowski trennen
spiegel.description: Zwei Köche, eine Symbiose: Der Aufstieg der Salt-&-Silver-Gründer Johannes Riffelmacher und Thomas Kosikowski wirkte wie eine Party. Nun trennen sie sich, sprechen erstmals über Kosikowskis Alkoholsucht – und unüberwindbare Differenzen.

spiegel.title: New York: Tishman Speyer investiert in Chrysler-Gebäude
spiegel.description: Auch wegen des Denkmalschutzes gestaltete sich die Suche nach einem Käufer langwierig. Nun will das Immobilienunternehmen Tishman Speyer 235 Millionen US-Dollar in den Wolkenkratzer investieren.

spiegel.title: Haustiere: Mit Hunden das Bett zu teilen, macht Schlaf nicht schlechter
spiegel.description: Mal wieder hundemüde? Viele Frauchen und Herrchen schlafen mit ihrem Haustier im Bett, auch wenn sie morgens das Gefühl haben, dadurch oft wach geworden zu sein. Forschende haben das überprüft.

spiegel.title: Berlin Abgeordnetenhauswahl 2026: Müssten AfD und Linke je ein Mandat verlieren?
spiegel.description: Berlin hat gewählt – doch möglicherweise müssen AfD und Linke zwei sicher geglaubte Sitze im Abgeordnetenhaus wieder abgeben. Grund für die Verwirrung: ein schlampig reformiertes Gesetz.

spiegel.title: Sachsen: Sexistische Diskriminierung – Studie deckt Defizite bei Polizei auf
spiegel.description: Griffe unter den Rock, sexistische Sprüche, unerwünschte Kontakte: Eine Studie der Uni Leipzig beschreibt vielfältige Formen von Sexismus bei der sächsischen Polizei. Auch beim Umgang mit Fehlverhalten sehen die Forschenden Defizite.

spiegel.title: Antisemitismus in Deutschland: Zwei Juden streiten über Gefahr von links und rechts

phys-org.description: Will higher sin taxes, and therefore higher prices, on candy, soft drinks and beer lead to more cross-border shopping? The answer is often assumed to be yes in the public debate, where one of the main arguments against sin taxes on unhealthy products has long been that higher prices will encourage more Danes to shop across the border.

phys-org.title: Emotional ties to cultural heritage show strongest link to digital museum engagement
phys-org.description: Museums are increasingly using digital technologies to create more interactive and accessible experiences for visitors. Technologies such as three-dimensional (3D) digital models, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) allow visitors to explore artifacts in new ways, both online and during visits to physical museums.

phys-org.title: Digital finance research maps psychology, algorithms, and risk
phys-org.description: A study of almost 1,000 research papers in the field of digital finance has mapped out how technology, investor behavior and financial market risk are connected. The work identified three distinct foundations rather than a single framework, with implications for understanding how psychological factors influence financial decisions and how to develop viable algorithms that provide automated investment guidance.

phys-org.title: Rising seas threaten the world's migratory shorebirds
phys-org.description: Birds undertake some of the world's most impressive migrations, traveling hundreds to thousands of kilometers every year in search of safe breeding grounds and seasonally abundant food resources. For many birds, migration is the key to their success. However, migration can also make species more vulnerable to threats.

phys-org.title: Five ways to enjoy fashion as a hobby without indulging in overconsumption
phys-org.description: Fashion lovers are generally associated with bursting wardrobes and chasing the latest trends. But that reputation is beginning to shift.

phys-org.title: How Spain's torrential rainstorms put sewage into its rivers and seas
phys-org.description: After heavy rain, Spanish cities often awaken to refreshed air and clean streets, while the rainwater itself vanishes into storm drains along with everything it swept away. Underground, however, a very different story unfolds.

phys-org.title: Snowball Earth's iron deposits may have formed through microbes living without sunlight
phys-org.description: Iron is one of the most abundant metals on Earth's surface, yet how such massive iron ore deposits formed throughout geological history has long remained a mystery. The prevailing theory has been that ancient photosynthetic bacteria oxidized iron, causing it to precipitate and accumulate in the oceans.

phys-org.title: From jargon to impact: Teaching undergraduates the art of public communication
phys-org.description: Articles published in The Conversation go well beyond academics writing for a general audience—they can also serve as valuable content for educators to use in the classroom.

phys-org.title: Cost of Canadian wildfires could top $2 trillion over the 21st century, study shows
phys-org.description: Failure to curb global warming now could cost future generations of Canadians trillions of dollars in wildfire impacts alone, according to a new Simon Fraser University study. The study is among the first to put a price tag on projected Canadian wildfire activity driven by climate change.

phys-org.title: Tiny photosynthetic organisms help transport carbon to the depths of the Baltic Sea
phys-org.description: Tiny photosynthetic organisms in the Baltic Sea can contribute substantially to the transport of carbon from surface waters to deeper parts of the sea. A new study from the Department of Ecology, Environment and Plant Sciences at Stockholm University shows that their ability to form colonies and aggregates is an important factor determining how much of their biomass sinks.

phys-org.description: A visualization of a dark moon eclipsing the sun is marked with handwritten notes in this April 6, 2026, screenshot from an Artemis II crew member's tablet.

phys-org.title: How a harmful bacterium senses iron—and why it matters for fighting infections
phys-org.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common culprit in hospital-acquired bacterial infections and is growing more resistant to antibiotics. New findings from Aaron Smith, professor of chemistry and biochemistry at UMBC, and collaborators at Oklahoma State University show how a two-protein system inside the bacterium operates like a sensitive switch: The pair detects iron both outside and inside the cell and then rewrites large parts of the microbe's metabolism in response.

phys-org.title: International experience gives business leaders an edge, study finds
phys-org.description: Business leaders with international experience play a significant role in shaping the success of their organizations and are often associated with stronger organizational performance, including higher growth, profitability and stock market performance, according to a new study published in the Journal of Management.

phys-org.title: Superbug P. aeruginosa uses two protein plugs to seal channels against antibiotics
phys-org.description: A joint research team has identified a new mechanism underlying antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major multidrug-resistant "superbug." The discovery provides important clues for the development of new treatments for multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The findings are published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Chain reaction that begins when tumor suppression gene is switched off offers clues to how cancer develops
phys-org.description: A tumor suppressor gene known as p53 is mutated in more than half of all cancers, but how it acts to prevent cancer formation is largely unknown. A study by UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers sheds light on this phenomenon by showing what happens when p53 becomes disabled, revealing the gene's diverse roles in maintaining healthy metabolic activity, repressing mobile genes called retrotransposons and preventing cells from adopting features of sperm and eggs.

phys-org.title: Nobel physics winner's pride at pioneering AI role
phys-org.description: Francis Halzen, winner of the Nobel Prize in physics, spoke with pride on Wednesday about his early promotion of artificial intelligence in his research on neutrinos.

phys-org.title: Offshore wind turbine foundations may cool ocean surface by mixing seawater
phys-org.description: New research within the PELAgIO ECOWind project has revealed how offshore wind farms can influence ocean temperatures and mixing, and why their effects depend on local conditions.

phys-org.description: Elementary school teachers often put such care into creating their classroom libraries: shelving multiple copies of each book, stringing lights around them to set the mood, situating beanbag chairs and magic carpet squares strategically to encourage students to settle in.

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
proj-syn.description: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

proj-syn.title: Closing NATO’s Deterrence Gap
proj-syn.description: With Russian provocations against NATO member states growing more frequent, the alliance urgently needs to develop a credible doctrine of punitive deterrence to guide its response to acts of aggression that fall below the threshold of war. Mere territorial defense is not enough.

proj-syn.title: The India-Pakistan Cold War
proj-syn.description: The current stalemate between India and Pakistan should be viewed not as a pause between rounds of negotiation, but rather as part of a deliberate Indian strategy of disengagement. India will return to the negotiating table only after Pakistan dismantles, comprehensively and verifiably, its state-supported terrorist networks.

proj-syn.title: The Next Era of Reform Must Be About Capability
proj-syn.description: Economic development should no longer be measured solely by how much finance is mobilized or how much fiscal space is created. It must also be judged by whether countries emerge more capable of setting their own priorities, responding to challenges, and seizing new opportunities to shape their own future.

proj-syn.title: With AI, Sharing Is Caring
proj-syn.description: Although the public's distrust of Big Tech is understandable, given past experience, that is not a reason to starve AI models of the information and data they will need to be useful. If serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on the technology's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.

proj-syn.title: Why the US-China Trade Truce Matters
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump’s agreement to extend their trade truce reflects the fact that both sides have leverage over the other. In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, the current fragile equilibrium may be the best one can hope for.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Voters Have Moved
proj-syn.description: A strong performance by the right-wing, Donald Trump-aligned candidate in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election demonstrates that the left-wing ruling party has failed to keep up with the times. The Brazilian electorate is older, more devout, and more preoccupied with crime and personal security than it once was.

proj-syn.title: Does Inclusive Finance Really Need Stablecoins?
proj-syn.description: Today, 1.3 billion adults—more than half of them women—remain excluded from the formal financial system, and lower-income consumers still struggle to find and access the financial products and services they need. Contrary to much hype, stablecoins are not the best way to solve either of these problems.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Election Debacle Is Lula’s Fault
proj-syn.description: Brazil's left has just suffered a crushing election defeat and will most likely lose the presidency at the end of October. The causes are many, beginning with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's longstanding refusal to groom an appealing successor.

proj-syn.title: Sino-American Stability Without Trust
proj-syn.description: The main outcomes of the Trump-Xi summit—the two-month trade extension, the dialogue on AI, and even the carefully chosen language on Taiwan—point to Sino-American relations being in a holding pattern. For both sides, the main task is to prevent managed rivalry from devolving into outright confrontation.

proj-syn.title: Iran’s Moment of Opportunity
proj-syn.description: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. But as justified as the Iranian leadership might feel in pursuing an obstinately maximalist strategy, it must be careful not to mistake short-term advantages for longer-term gains.

proj-syn.title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?
proj-syn.description: When Russia replaced the Soviet Union as a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council in 1991, it did not even attempt to follow the process outlined in the UN Charter. Now that Russia’s usurpation of the USSR’s seat has enabled it to wage a war of aggression, the dubious legal status of its position must be revisited.

proj-syn.title: To Support Nepal, Waive Remittance Fees
proj-syn.description: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

proj-syn.title: What a Canada–Europe Alliance Needs
proj-syn.description: With trade, finance, technology, and supply chains having all become instruments of coercion, Canada, Europe, and other likeminded democracies must come together to defend their interests. But strategic convergence between governments is not enough; if a new alliance is to endure, it needs deep roots in society.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean

crunchbase.title: There Was Never An Easy AI Era, And Investors Are Raising The Bar
crunchbase.description: As AI IPOs bring greater scrutiny, argues guest author Maor Farid, founder and CEO of Leo AI, investors will increasingly prioritize customer spending growth, sustainable margins and deployment efficiency over rapid revenue growth alone.

crunchbase.title: North America’s Startup Funding Falls In Q3 As AI Giants Eye The Public Markets
crunchbase.description: In total, investors poured $92 billion into seed- through growth-stage rounds for U.S. and Canadian startups in the third quarter, per Crunchbase data. That’s a 35% decline from the prior quarter but up 50% from year-ago levels.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows AI’s Most Active Startups Are Becoming Serial Acquirers
crunchbase.description: Some of the AI industry’s fastest-growing startups are becoming serial acquirers, buying smaller companies to fill product gaps, enter new markets and bring specialized teams in-house, a review of Crunchbase data shows. While AI giant OpenAI is by far the busiest of these buyers, well-funded startups in legal tech, customer service and software development have also made multiple acquisitions this year.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows. And while the third quarter was the lowest for startup investment so far this year, it still exceeded every other quarter since Q2 2022. We take a look at where the funding went.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Almost All About AI
crunchbase.description: This week’s list of the largest U.S. startup funding rounds was pretty much all about AI. That includes the biggest financing — a $1 billion round for Instinct, a developer of AI assistants for everyday tasks — as well as most of the rest of the Top 10.

crunchbase.title: Your Investors Can Make Or Break Your Startup. Here’s Who Founders Actually Need On Their Cap Table
crunchbase.description: For startup founders, the goal shouldn’t be assembling a cap table filled with whoever was willing to invest, but rather intentionally constructed around investors who bring different forms of value. Guest author Antonia Dean, a partner at Black Operator Ventures, shares three things founders should look for in their investors.

crunchbase.title: Nautical And Marine Startups See Stepped-Up Funding
